articles.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'

articles.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?

articles.title: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?

articles.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'

articles.title: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack

articles.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets

articles.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe

articles.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over

articles.title: Why AI researchers warn humanity could face extinction

articles.title: Iran and US: Two countries and the pistachio between them

articles.description: Germany thrilled fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup. But even if this sparked a boom in the women's game, the infrastructure simply isn't ready for it.
articles.title: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?

articles.title: Africa's richest man Dangote's IPO out of reach in Nigeria

articles.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?

articles.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?

articles.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn

articles.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter

articles.title: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: What's next for the sport?

articles.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace

articles.title: Werner Herzog: Germany's wild man of cinema is back

articles.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands

articles.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination

articles.title: How Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Kenan ‘Ken’ Urker, 34, who died of apparent drug overdose, was partner of woman convicted of murder of mother 
The on-and-off partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, who spent time in prison for her role in the murder of her abusive mother, was found dead inside his Louisiana home on his 34th birthday on Thursday in what authorities described as an apparent drug overdose.
The sheriff’s office in Lafourche parish, Louisiana, confirmed Kenan “Ken” Urker – the father of Blanchard’s daughter – was discovered on Thursday after relatives asked police to conduct a welfare check at his residence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard found dead in Louisiana home

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now); Abené Clayton, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Taz Ali (earlier)
articles.description:
President has claimed pipeline project was part of a deal made last year to lower tariffs on imports from South Korea in return for billions of dollars of investments in the US

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Send us your questions on how the Iran war will affect US voters in the midterms

And as we bring you the latest on how the jobs report stands to impact voter sentiment ahead of the November midterms, my colleagues have done all the hard work in mapping out the battle for Congress and the key states, candidates and districts that will ultimately decide the balance of power on Capitol Hill.
Many indicators of voter sentiment suggest the Democrats are favored to take back control of the House of Representatives, and potentially the Senate. Winning either would be a significant victory for the party and give it the power to block Trump’s legislative agenda and more aggressively investigate his administration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump threatens to double tariffs on South Korea if they do not pay for Alaska natural gas pipeline – US politics live

articles.author: Roque Planas
articles.description:
Plan to install barriers through popular national park sparked outrage from advocates and politicians alike
A federal judge has temporarily blocked the Trump administration from expanding the border wall and other security infrastructure across the Big Bend region of west Texas, where contentious plans to build roads and vehicle barriers through a popular national park have led to furious backlash and public protests.
US district judge Kathleen Cardone’s ruling after a Friday hearing in El Paso deals a major blow to the Trump administration’s efforts to expand the border wall through west Texas at breakneck pace, while riding roughshod over the objections of local business owners, landowners, public land advocates and politicians from both parties.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Federal judge halts Big Bend border wall construction in blow to Trump agenda

articles.author: Vikram Dodd and Hannah Al-Othman
articles.description:
Man, most likely in Iran, was in contact with men arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur, police say
Two Iranian men have been charged in relation to an alleged terror plot targeting Manchester’s Jewish community.
​Police say another man, most likely in Iran, was in contact with them as part of a plot to get a bomb to attack Jewish targets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two Iranian men charged over alleged terror plot targeting Manchester’s Jewish community

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Kevin Warsh’s predecessor had been investigated over cost overruns related to central bank renovation project
The US ⁠justice department is not reopening a criminal investigation into former Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell ⁠for cost overruns ⁠related ​to the central bank’s building renovation project, a department spokesperson said on Friday.
Attorney general Todd ⁠Blanche – in comments to Bloomberg News, which first reported the development – said he has not ruled out ⁠continuing to look into the project’s oversight and potentially take ​action if evidence of ‌wrongdoing came to ‌light.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: DoJ declines to reopen investigation into former Fed chair Jay Powell

articles.author: Alba Asenjo Domínguez in Washington
articles.description:
The justice and treasury departments said they sent $2m to Hamas through charities and cryptocurrency, while six people were arrested across the US and France
The Trump administration on Friday unveiled sanctions against three individuals allegedly related to the Islamist militant group Hamas and against two charities based in France while also announcing six arrests – actions that the government called an “extraordinary counter-terrorism work” to expose “a sophisticated, multi‑year financing architecture”.
Investigators alleged that the network moved more than $2m to Hamas “through deceptive charitable fronts and cryptocurrency channels”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US sanctions three individuals and two charities over alleged Hamas financing

articles.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
President leads huge rally in Rio before election on Sunday seen as most important for decades
The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has claimed he is the only thing standing in the way of far-right “fascists” reclaiming power, as he led a huge rally through the streets of Rio ahead of Sunday’s crunch election.
Speaking on the eve of the demonstration, the 80-year-old leftwinger said he had decided to seek a historic fourth term because he believed only he could prevent the family of his rightwing rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, returning to government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil’s Lula says only he can stop rise of fascism under Bolsonaro’s son

articles.author: Martin Farrer
articles.description:
The epicentre was at Leongatha, 130km south-east of Melbourne, with residents reporting houses shaking just after 2am

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A magnitude 4.8 earthquake struck Victoria in the early hours of Saturday morning, shaking Melbourne and waking people across the whole region.
Geoscience Australia said it detected an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 4.8 at 2.01am near Leongatha, 130km south-east of Melbourne, with the tremors felt across the city’s eastern suburbs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Magnitude 4.8 earthquake hits Victoria with tremors felt across Melbourne

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Joshua Kerry, 28, of Rotherham in South Yorkshire, charged with one count of preparation of terrorist acts, say police
The man accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe has been charged with engaging in conduct in preparation of acts of terrorism including against Nigel Farage.
Joshua Kerry, 28, of Rotherham in South Yorkshire, was charged by the Crown Prosecution Service on Friday with one count of preparation of terrorist acts. The charge relates to activity alleged to have taken place between 31 May 2024 and 8 July this year, counter-terrorism police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ann Widdecombe murder suspect charged with planning terror act against Nigel Farage

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Buckingham Palace say the king will not ‘shy away’ from Britain’s role in slavery when he visits Commonwealth nations later this month
King Charles III will acknowledge the “darkest days” of colonial rule and slavery while touring Caribbean countries on a visit beginning this month, a Buckingham Palace spokesperson said on Friday.
The king will first visit the Bahamas and Guyana alone, followed by a trip with Queen Camilla to Antigua and Barbuda, where Charles will give a speech at a meeting of Commonwealth heads of government, the palace said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: King Charles III to acknowledge ‘darkest days’ of Britain’s colonial rule during Caribbean tour

articles.author: Joanna Partridge, Jillian Ambrose and Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Leaders agree a coordinated drawdown after surge in prices and Donald Trump’s threat to cut off US supplies
Leaders of G7 nations are to release up to 100m barrels of their emergency diesel and crude oil stockpiles after Donald Trump threatened to cut off supplies of US diesel.
The French President, Emmanuel Macron, said ministers from some of world’s largest economies had agreed to release stocks from their strategic oil reserves after crisis talks on Friday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: G7 to release up to 100m barrels of emergency oil and diesel reserves

articles.author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Five defendants accused of being part of ‘black team’ tasked with overcoming security at Israel-linked firm Elbit near Bristol
Palestine Action activists brandished whips, hammers and kebab skewers to intimidate security guards and keep them at bay during a break-in at an Israel-linked arms factory, a court has heard.
Five defendants are accused by prosecutors of being part of a “black team”, wearing black jumpsuits, whose role was to overwhelm security guards, so that a “red team”, wearing red jumpsuits, could break into the Elbit systems factory in Filton, near Bristol, and smash up equipment including drones.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Palestine Action activists used whips and hammers to threaten guards at arms factory, court hears

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Guarantee will remain until 2030 but MPs will vote on changes during this parliament, government says
Andy Burnham will pass legislation to scrap the state pension triple lock in this parliament, even though the guarantee will remain until 2030, the government has said.
The prime minister used his conference speech to announce a change to the policy, which guarantees that the state pension rises by the highest of 2.5%, inflation or earnings growth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to pass law scrapping pension triple lock before next election

articles.author: Ashifa Kassam in Madrid
articles.description:
Opposition lawmakers join forces to defeat proposals made by Socialist-led coalition after eviction of 87-year-old
Rightwing lawmakers in Spain have rejected emergency measures put forward to tackle the country’s housing crisis, pitting a fractured parliament against the widespread protest movement that has swelled in recent days.
On Friday Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist-led coalition put forward two decrees that included a range of measures aimed at improving access to housing, from a ban on evictions until 2030 to the regulation of temporary lettings and lettings by room.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spanish right wing votes down housing crisis plans as protest movement grows

articles.description:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here
Back to France, midday figures quoted by Le Figaro show that 564 schools and educational establishments have been disrupted by the ongoing unrest, and some 600 people have been arrested so far today as the high school protests continue.
Europe environment correspondent
 Continue reading...
articles.title: G7 to release 100m barrels from reserves to combat surging diesel prices – as it happened

articles.author: Jason Burke International security correspondent
articles.description:
Experts sceptical flydubai co-pilot’s only motivation was to end his own life and say key question is means of radicalisation
At about 9.30 on Wednesday morning local time, Tali Manes was taking her six-year-old daughter, Nina, to the toilet on the regular flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv when she heard a series of heavy blows against the cockpit door.
Manes, an Israeli bank executive, immediately told a flight attendant seated nearby that something was wrong. When he did not react, she shouted at him: “Something is happening in there!” Seconds later, the man “simply went to the [cockpit] door and opened it”, Manes told Israel’s Channel 12 TV.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Suicide by plane or terrorism? Speculation over motive in flight 1073 attack

articles.author: Reuters in Washington
articles.description:
US says ship thought to be using common ‘dark fleet’ tactics was boarded and taken to Mexico as embargo continues
The US Coast ⁠Guard has announced that it intercepted a large cargo ship carrying fuel bound for Cuba, as the ⁠Trump administration’s crippling ⁠oil embargo against ​the island nation continued.
The vessel named Grace was stopped on 5 September in the Caribbean Sea between Cuba ⁠and Mexico while using tactics to evade authorities, the Coast Guard said. The New York Times reported that the ship ⁠was 91 metres (300ft) long.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US Coast Guard says it intercepted ship carrying fuel to Cuba

articles.author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
articles.description:
Home affairs department orders all federal government agencies to conduct review of ‘legacy technology’ amid fallout from AI agent hacks 

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian government faces significant “tech debt” that could bring a big bill for taxpayers after the OpenAI Medicare breach, as government agencies will need to fortify their defences against future attacks by AI agents.
This week, the home affairs department ordered all federal government agencies to conduct a “legacy technology stocktake” that requires a plan for each agency to “reduce legacy technology systems” to a level within the agency’s risk tolerance and appetite, the direction stated.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: OpenAI’s Medicare attack has exposed Australia’s ‘tech debt’. Fixing it could bring a big bill for taxpayers

articles.author: Pjotr Sauer in Kyiv
articles.description:
Mayor Vitali Klitschko says Kyivans can no longer pretend it is ‘peacetime’ amid strikes on school, hospital and bridge
Valeriya Tkachenko was dropping her son off at school in central Kyiv when the air raid alert sounded. Staff hurried the children and parents into the shelter, where the frightened lawyer spent the next two hours with her son.
“I’m scared to death all day about what could happen to my son,” she said as she emerged from the shelter, already late for work.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The enemy is tearing our city apart’: terror in Kyiv as Russia ramps up attacks

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Mumbai
articles.description:
Thousands gather in Mumbai with heavy police presence as concerns mount that millions will be denied voting rights
India’s youth-led Cockroach movement kicked off more nationwide protests on Friday as thousands of people gathered in Mumbai, amid mounting concerns that millions of citizens are being unfairly stripped of their vote.
The movement, which calls itself the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) and has massive support among the country’s gen Zs, returned to the streets to demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement launches new protests over changes to voter roll

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Government struggling to deal with worst crisis in months after being taken by surprise by massive demonstrations
As dozens of school pupils sat on top of a pile of wheelie bins blocking a high school entrance in north-eastern Paris, Sophia, 17, was on the frontline of the barricade, when she would normally have been attending Spanish class.
“We hope this grows into a massive youth protest movement,” said the final year baccalaureate student at Paris’s Lycée Voltaire, who did not want her real name published. She was on her second day of blocking the school entrance along with hundreds of others, ensuring all lessons were cancelled. “We just want to be listened to by the government. We’d rather stand here doing this than have to learn in poor conditions. It’s the only way to make ourselves heard.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fires, fury and hundreds of arrests as France gripped by student protests

articles.author: Henry Belot
articles.description:
Baird, father of former NSW premier Mike Baird and journalist Julia Baird, helped win the Olympics for Sydney

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Bruce Baird, a former federal Liberal MP and deputy leader of the party’s New South Wales branch, has died aged 84.
Baird, who also served as the NSW transport minister from 1988 to 1995, is the father of former state premier Mike Baird, the ABC journalist Julia Baird, and the marketing executive Steve Baird.

articles.title: Bruce Baird, former federal Liberal MP and NSW minister, dies aged 84

articles.author: Henry Belot
articles.description:
Attack accessing historical data on bushfires occurred in June but not disclosed by the tech company until Thursday

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Artificial intelligence company OpenAI has disclosed another unauthorised hack on a government department in Australia.
In June, an OpenAI agent hacked into a New South Wales state government department and accessed historical non-public data on bushfires without authorisation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: OpenAI disclose another hack on government department in Australia

articles.author: Hanaa Hammad in Cairo
articles.description:
Artwork created in Tahrir Square for Chinese president’s state visit to Egypt is painted over amid allegations it revived Afrocentric claims about pharaohs’ origins
On the eve of the Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight.
Depicting the Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti, the painting was among 40 murals commissioned to beautify the city for Xi’s arrival and was painted by a group of young volunteers, Rasmet Basma, in Tahrir Square.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up ‘passengers would lose their lives’
The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life.
Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I was fighting for my life’: Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls flydubai cockpit attack

articles.author: Jordyn Beazley
articles.description:
Under new WA laws anyone who defies an exclusion order could face a maximum $36,000 fine and three years in prison

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Activists and a Greens MP have threatened legal action after the Western Australia police banned at least 12 people entering a designated security area where the Land Forces weapons expo will be held in Perth from 6 October.
The police used special powers given to them by the WA government last month to ban the activists from entering the area surrounding the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Activists plan legal action against police ban on entering security zone near Perth weapons expo

articles.author: Libby Brooks
articles.description:
In today’s newsletter: When a passenger plane plunges 17,000ft amid claims of terrorism, hijacking and geopolitical intrigue, Guardian journalists have to try and separate fact from fiction in real time
Good morning. Shocking news of a cockpit stabbing. Graphic footage of bloodied crew members. Mid-air testimony from terrified passengers.
This was the tenor of the heart-in-mouth reporting as the horrifying events unfolded onboard flight FZ 1073 to Tel Aviv: the early morning budget flight that plummeted 17,000ft in under two minutes before the courageous intervention of passengers and crew averted an apparent hijacking, potentially saving the lives of not just the 170+ passengers and crew on board, but many more.
UK politics | Ministers are working up sweeping plans for welfare changes including scrapping a key disability benefit for under-25s and replacing it with a multibillion-pound package of support to get into work.
Northern Ireland | Talks aimed at resolving the Drumcree parade dispute have broken up without agreement, with Northern Ireland secretary Chris Bryant describing the situation as being between a “rock and a hard place”.
US news | Tennessee’s governor has suspended all executions in the state and ordered an independent inquiry after a botched attempt to put a condemned inmate to death on Wednesday night.
AI | When prompted, AI chat bots will edit images to remove the hijabs from Muslim women, a violation of one of the world’s most common and visible expressions of faith.
Europe news | A fast-growing protest by high-school students over long hours, teacher shortages and decaying facilities has escalated into “urban violence”, the French government has warned.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Friday briefing: How we covered the flydubai incident as it unfolded

articles.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Speculation that Flávio Bolsonaro will try to strip Our Lady of Aparecida of position could become deciding factor in run-up to Sunday
A row of Biblical proportions has erupted in the run-up to Brazil’s presidential election, with the country’s patron saint, Our Lady of Aparecida, emerging as an unlikely kingmaker in the deadlocked race.
Ahead of Sunday’s vote, the two frontrunners – the leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and his far-right challenger, Flávio Bolsonaro – are level in the polls.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No one disrespects Our Lady’: fears for Brazil’s patron saint grip country ahead of election

articles.author: Presented by Annie Kelly with Tom Phillips; produced by Guy Szafman and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent and Homa Khaleeli
articles.description:
Latin America correspondent Tom Phillips reports on this Sunday’s historic presidential elections in Brazil, as the son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro hopes to take power
You would have been forgiven for thinking that when Jair Bolsonaro was convicted in September 2025 of attempting a coup, his political career was finished and his legacy forever tainted.
But in the first round of Brazil’s presidential elections this Sunday, another Bolsonaro has genuine hopes of victory – not Jair, but his son Flávio, who ialso campaigning to have his father released released.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Bolsonaros…they’re back! Brazil heads to the polls – podcast

articles.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro, Andrew Roth and Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Jorge Messias calls Guardian report ‘an important alert for Brazilian sovereignty’ as nation prepares to go to polls
Brazil’s attorney general has said foreign meddling in his country’s institutions and democracy “cannot be tolerated” after a Guardian report revealed how the Trump administration was pushing to direct funds to a campaign against the Brazilian supreme court.
Writing on X, Jorge Messias called the report “an important alert for Brazilian sovereignty”. “The information is especially serious in light of Brazil’s electoral process and the recent episodes of external pressure on our institutions,” Messias added.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil attorney general says meddling ‘cannot be tolerated’ after Trump funding plans revealed

articles.author: Peter Beaumont
articles.description:
Team behind documentary push back against IDF attempt to discredit its exposure of military systems
The team behind the award-winning film NAZA, which details the Israeli military’s targeting policies in Gaza and its alleged acceptance of high numbers of civilian deaths, have revealed they spoke to more than 100 sources with knowledge of the military systems used in the war.
The disclosure came in response to an Israel Defense Forces statement seeking to discredit the documentary.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NAZA film-makers say they spoke to more than 100 sources about Israeli actions in Gaza

articles.author: William Christou and Jonathan Yerushalmy
articles.description:
Alleged flydubai attacker interrogated by Saudi security services as investigation into apparent crash attempt opens
The Omani co-pilot who stabbed his captain in an apparent attempt to crash an Israel-bound flight from Dubai had previously undergone radical Islamist indoctrination and was suicidal, Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has claimed.
Israeli passengers intervened to stop the attack on Wednesday, restraining the co-pilot, while a reserve crew in the plane was able to stabilise the plummeting plane and ultimately land it safely in Saudi Arabia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Co-pilot in flight stabbing had ‘Islamic radical indoctrination’, says Netanyahu

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Indian government issued with warning it would be in contempt of court if it failed to release Jagtar Singh Johal
The British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal has been released from a Delhi prison after the Indian high court warned the government it would be found in contempt of court if it continued to attempt to keep him in jail despite an 18 September court order releasing him on bail. Johal has been incarcerated for nine years without any full trial.
The court order was issued after Johal’s lawyers issued a writ of habeas corpus alleging he was being detained against the express direction of the court.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Sikh activist released from Delhi jail after nine-year detention

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Estonian completed first of two attempts to navigate narrow ribbon, 160 metres long and 120 metres high, near the city’s famous Gyeongbokgung palace on Thursday
The lunchtime crowds drifted slowly back to their offices along central Seoul’s main boulevard, heads up and phones raised to the sky.
High above, a narrow ribbon ran between the Koreana hotel and the Dong-A Media Center, a few hundred metres from the capital’s famous Gyeongbokgung palace and Gwanghwamun square.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Daredevil Jaan Roose completes slackline walk high above central Seoul

articles.author: Andrew Roth and Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Support such as for white Afrikaners and anti-communism reveals how US is redefining what qualifies as human rights
With hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court and programs that would reward ideological allies in Europe who protect “western civilizational norms”.
On Wednesday, the state department obligated the funds to the grantees hours before the deadline despite congressional concerns and requests not to do so, according to a source familiar with the negotiations. The state department declined to comment on questions from the Guardian specifically on whether it had obligated the funds and had “blown” holds from Congress due to concerns about the money’s use.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Women say nothing has changed since Delhi’s infamous Nirbhaya bus rape case 14 years ago
The posters, just like the women holding them, were taking no prisoners. “Girls don’t need curfews, rapists need consequences,” read one. “Lock your dicks rather than your women at home,” read another.
As hundreds of women walked from the gates of their university campus into the streets of Delhi – where sexual harassment, assault, catcalling and molestation are a constant, daily threat – they shouted together in a chorus of rage and defiance: “We want justice.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We want justice’: series of rapes trigger mass protests at Indian universities

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
President announces measures amid anger at authorities over recent murders of women
South Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders.
Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women. He said police would be reviewing unsolved murders, attempted murders and serious sexual offences against women and children, as well as producing a funded plan to reduce the forensic backlog for such cases, both within 60 days.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings

articles.author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
articles.description:
Institutions have for years turned to China for funding opportunities but national security concerns are mounting

MI5 issues spy alert to UK universities over Chinese front company stealing research

The security alert issued by MI5 regarding a Chinese state-owned conglomerate accused of conducting espionage in the UK reveals the extent to which British intelligence remains concerned about Beijing’s influence, and risks casting a shadow over UK-China cooperation at a time when the bilateral relationship is enjoying a revival.
The UK’s domestic security service on Wednesday warned researchers and academics to cease work with the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), an organisation MI5 described as a “significant threat”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities

articles.author: Vikram Dodd, Sally Weale, Simon Goodley and Richard Adams
articles.description:
Security service says academics should stop working with and taking grants from firm backed by Chinese intelligence

MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities

MI5 has issued a rare public warning to UK universities that China’s intelligence service is using a front company to pay for research by UK academics and steal the secrets of hi-tech projects.
Britain’s domestic security service said researchers and academics should cease work with the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI), sometimes also known as the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT).
Additional reporting by Helena Horton
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MI5 warns UK universities over ‘theft of tech secrets by Chinese front company’

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Burundi joins several other African nations in accepting people deported under Trump’s hardline policy
Burundi has agreed to join a clutch of ⁠other African nations in receiving migrants from other countries deported from the US under ⁠Donald Trump’s hardline ⁠immigration ​policy.
However, Burundi will only accept those not accused of crime or terrorism links, said ⁠Nancy Ninette Mutoni, a spokesperson for the country’s president, Évariste Ndayishimiye. Tuesday’s announcement gave no details of numbers, timing or financial ⁠details.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burundi agrees to receive ‘third-country’ migrant deportees from US

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
Kenjiro Tsuda wins case against TikTok account in landmark Japanese verdict to protect publicity rights
A court in Japan has ruled that the human voice has legal protection after a landmark case involving a well-known actor and a TikTok account that he claimed had cloned his “lustrous” baritone voice in its AI-generated videos.
Tokyo district court said on Wednesday that voices should enjoy the same protection as publicity rights, at the end of a closely watched legal action brought against TikTok by Kenjiro Tsuda – best known for voicing the character Kento Nanami in the anime Jujutsu Kaisen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI tool that copied actor’s ‘lustrous’ voice violated his rights, Tokyo court rules

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Blast during search operation near border fuels political tensions amid attempts to revive diplomatic channels
South Korea has demanded an apology from North Korea over a landmine blast that injured three soldiers, saying they were hurt by North Korean mines on the southern side of the border.
Kang Hyun-woo, the director of operations at South Korea’s joint chiefs of staff, demanded an apology and “responsible measures” from Pyongyang over the blast, which occurred on 21 September during a search operation south of the border.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South Korea calls for apology from North Korea after mine injures three soldiers

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
As outrage grows over cases​ of sexual violence, activists are demanding a shift from controlling women to confronting men’s behaviour. Plus, Tony Klor’s ‘hella dope’ city vlogs
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
As an Indian woman, I often feel myself oscillating between states of anxiety or anger. The anxiety is about doing the mental maths of how to stay safe – thinking about what I’m wearing, where I am going and how I’ll get there, and so on. The anger is at the sheer absurdity of this, and the stories of of sexual violence and harassment I read about every day. I am not the only one.
Last week, two particularly enraging incidents captured national attention. First, a video showing a group of men accused of harassing and molesting two teenagers at night in Bihar’s Jamui went viral. Then, a 17-year-old, out with a friend in Delhi, was allegedly gang-raped in a park by men posing as police. After, women in Bihar told Outlook how the incident in Jamui triggers greater controls and pressure on them. In Delhi, authorities curbed access to public parks and a premier women’s college, Lady Shri Ram College (LSR), briefly moved classes online.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From Jamui to Delhi, the burden of safety from sexual assault cannot fall on women

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Marie-Celestin Karondwa was attacked on Sunday after promoting measures to prevent spread of disease, his party says

A senior member of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ruling party was beaten to death on Sunday after appearing on a radio programme to raise awareness about the Ebola outbreak, a party representative has said.
Marie-Celestin Karondwa, the acting president of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party’s federal executive committee in Butembo, a new hotspot for the outbreak, was attacked after taking part in a ​radio show during which he ‌promoted prevention measures for the disease, ‌the UDPS federation in the city said in a statement, Reuters reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: DRC politician beaten to death after radio appearance about Ebola outbreak

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Tens of thousands of police deployed and roads barricaded as PTI party demands release of jailed former PM
Leaders from Imran Khan’s party have vowed to go ahead with a nationwide demonstration in Pakistan to demand the former prime minister’s release, even as the government deployed tens of thousands of police to Islamabad, barricaded highways and issued arrest warrants to try to stop the march.
The state has taken extreme measures to prevent Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party from proceeding with the march. It was announced after mounting concerns of the treatment of Khan, who has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan locks down Islamabad as Imran Khan’s party vows to march on capital

articles.author: Jamie Driscoll
articles.description:
Imagine the UK with a 20-year investment plan, with green homes and fast transport. We already have the tools to make it happen
You’ve just left school. What’s your future?
I know a physics graduate making flat whites; a 30-year-old living in his childhood bedroom who feels like a failure; a lad in Blyth who turned down a job 15 miles away because there’s no bus, and for young people his age car insurance is almost £2,000 a year. Britain’s young people are our greatest resource, and we are failing them because capital markets won’t allocate investment where it is needed. Saying “hope” in a conference speech sounds warm. But people need a plan.
Jamie Driscoll is a Green party councillor on Newcastle city council and former North of Tyne mayor
 Continue reading...
articles.title: There is a way to look after people, the planet – and Britain’s growth. It’s what we call the ‘wellbeing economy’ | Jamie Driscoll

articles.author: Megan Davies and James Michelin for MetDesk
articles.description:
Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring landslides and deaths in Nepal
Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.
Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, are most at risk. Valencia has experienced several damaging floods in recent years. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Eastern Spain braces for torrential rain and flooding

articles.author: Joanna Ruck
articles.description:
This week’s best wildlife photographs from around the world
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The week in wildlife: a rescued orangutan, the chonkiest bear and a barn owl’s triumph

articles.author: Gary Fuller
articles.description:
‘Day-to-day’ symptom of harmful emissions, which in turn can disrupt sleep, can be overlooked, say researchers
New research has found that increased air pollution is associated with more night-time coughing, leading to disturbed sleep.
Most air pollution research looks at symptoms that are severe enough for people to seek medical help, but day-to-day symptoms can be overlooked. Prof Cecilia Mascolo, who led the study from the University of Cambridge, said: “I come from an area in Italy with very high pollution and I am very aware of its not-talked-about effects.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Increased air pollution linked to more night-time coughing, UK-led study finds

articles.author: Ajit Niranjan
articles.description:
EU Copernicus report shows surface air temperatures from June to August were 2.5C above decadal average
The scorching heat that persistently baked western Europe this summer was the worst on record, a report has found, with more than half the continent seared by “very strong” heat stress that felt hotter than 38C.
Surface air temperatures in western Europe from June to August were 2.5C above the recent decadal average, according to an update from the EU’s Copernicus climate monitoring service on Friday, while milder but still deadly heat across the rest of the continent made the summer Europe’s third hottest on record.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: May heatwaves, deaths, ruined harvests: study of Europe’s summer paints grim picture for the future

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Democratic-led coalition says gutting key protections will set US back decades and worsen climate crisis
States and cities sued the Trump administration on Thursday for repealing rules that limit planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants fueled by coal and natural gas.
Twenty-one states, led by New York, are challenging the Environmental Protection Agency’s power plant rule. The Democratic-led coalition also includes Pennsylvania’s governor, the District of Columbia, New York City, Chicago and the city and county of Denver. They argue that “gutting one of the country’s most significant climate protections” will set the nation back decades and worsen the climate crisis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US states and cities sue over Trump EPA’s repeal of emissions rules

articles.author: Ben Tracy of Climate Central
articles.description:
Lake Mead is at its lowest level since it was filled nearly 90 years ago, Lake Powell also at a historic low
It was 42C (108F) degrees as we motored across Nevada’s Lake Mead in our rented pontoon boat. Colby Pellegrino with the Southern Nevada Water Authority wanted to show us something we shouldn’t have been able to see. She pointed toward a rock island where a large metal pipe was sticking out of the water.
“That is the first intake that was built to bring municipal water into the valley in 1970,” Pellegrino said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Colorado River is shrinking. What happens next?

articles.author: Adam Morton, Graham Readfearn and Penry Buckley
articles.description:
Exclusive: Climate Change Authority chair says planning commission did not account for climate-related economic damage in NSW

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

A senior Albanese government climate adviser has challenged the state approval of the largest coalmining development in New South Wales’s history, arguing “climate change isn’t someone else’s problem”.
Matt Kean, the chair of the Climate Change Authority and a former NSW treasurer and energy minister, questioned why the state Independent Planning Commission had not weighed the economic cost of climate change caused by burning the coal from the Hunter Valley Operations mine before giving it the green light to run until 2045.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Matt Kean warns climate crisis ‘isn’t someone else’s problem’ as largest coal project in NSW history greenlit

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
As the midterms approach, Americans’ digestive health has become a bizarre talking point
Donald Trump seems to spend an unusual amount of time thinking about toilets.
Back in 2019, he bizarrely claimed: “People are flushing toilets 10 times, 15 times as opposed to once.” He repeated this claim at a Michigan rally the following year. “Ten times, right, 10 times,” Trump complained. “Not me, of course not me, but you,” he added while pointing at an unfortunate audience member.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is Trump to blame for Americans getting explosive diarrhea? | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Evan Simon of Floodlight
articles.description:
Records show Vineland facility in New Jersey emitted health-harming pollution before regulators stepped in
DataOne, the Microsoft-linked New Jersey datacenter recently hit with a $1m fine for running unpermitted generators, emitted large amounts of health-harming air pollution for nearly a year before state regulators stepped in, according to public records obtained by Floodlight.
The Vineland facility’s 62 gas-fired generators became public in August after a Floodlight/Guardian visual investigation found them operating without permits. The New Jersey department of environmental protection last week fined the company over the fleet but did not disclose how long the generators had been operating nor how much air pollution they had released into the surrounding community over the past year.
This story is from Floodlight, a non-profit newsroom that investigates the powers stalling climate action. Sign up for Floodlight’s newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US datacenter discharged large amounts of pollution for almost a year with no permits

articles.author: Oliver Milman
articles.description:
Gavin Newsom says Trump is a ‘gift’ to the climate cause for dispelling notions of fossil fuel energy security

Send us your questions about how the Iran war will affect US voters in the midterms

Of all the epithets hurled at Donald Trump since he became US president, perhaps the most unusual was delivered last week – that he is, in fact, some sort of environmentalist.
Trump is the “greatest gift” to the environmental movement, argued Gavin Newsom, California’s governor, due to the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump the environmentalist? How his Iran war exposed the fragility of dirty energy

articles.author: Rebecca Ratcliffe
articles.description:
The global climate phenomenon has triggered devastating infernos in the ape’s Indonesian heartlands, with long-term effects on the animals still unknown
The mother’s hands were peeling from walking on the torched ground. Her eight-month-old baby, which clung to her side, was dehydrated and thin. The pair, named Mama Abu and Abu (“ash” in Indonesian), were found in an oil palm subsidiary estate, rescuers say.
The orangutan pair were saved last month from wildfires that are devouring Indonesia’s forests and peatland, unleashing thick smog, and destroying the habitat of some of the planet’s most vulnerable species.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The toll is huge’: El Niño-driven wildfires overwhelm Indonesia’s orangutan population

articles.author: Georgina Woods
articles.description:
There is no greater treachery than this failure to face up to the climate crisis. How can we now fend off despair?
The Independent Planning Commission’s published reasons for approving the largest coalmine in New South Wales history in the context of mounting death, disaster and despair brought on by global heating reads like a hostage statement.
In its decision, the commission accepts that the extension of the Hunter Valley Operations’ mine for a further 19 years – resulting 809m tonnes of greenhouse gas pollution – will materially worsen global warming. The panel members cite CSIRO’s finding that climate change is having a growing effect on the lives and livelihoods of all Australians and that the severity of that impact “will depend on the speed at which global greenhouse gas emissions can be reduced”. They reject the idea that keeping HVO’s coal in the ground would make no difference to global warming.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The green light for the largest coalmine in NSW history is shocking proof that our governance systems are betraying Australians | Georgina Woods

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
Sunday’s general election is too close to call, with the incumbent president facing the son of the man who attempted a coup against him
Sunday’s election in Brazil could hardly be a clearer-cut choice – nor a closer call. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known as Lula, is neck and neck in the polls with Flávio Bolsonaro, the son and champion of the jailed far-right former president Jair. Mr Bolsonaro senior is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup to “annihilate” democracy after losing the last election.
Brazil is Latin America’s largest democracy, but military dictatorship is in its recent past. Mr Bolsonaro wants to free his father and those who rioted in his support in 2023. The senator has campaigned as a less crass and temperamental version of his father, but he is no less extreme. For many on both sides, this is a vote against a man they detest more than an endorsement of their own candidate. Most voters disapprove of both men.
Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on Lula v the Bolsonaros: the decision of Brazilian voters will affect us all | Editorial

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Images of gliding king penguins, a sugar thief rosella and a bin brush turkey are among the winning and shortlisted photos in this year’s prize. Funds raised by the competition support bird conservation programs in Australia

Australia’s best photos the month – September 2026

 Continue reading...
articles.title: The 2026 BirdLife Australia photography awards – in pictures

articles.author: Gabrielle Canon in San Francisco
articles.description:
Wave nearing southern California expected to reach San Francisco Bay Area by October as it crawls toward Alaska
Communities across California are rushing to prepare for the imminent arrival of the so-called “Kelvin wave”, a massive underwater band of warm water threatening to inundate swaths of the vast North American shoreline.
The wave is nearing southern California and expected to reach the San Francisco Bay Area by early October, as it crawls toward Alaska. Waters could rise by a foot along the California coast, according to scientists, who have warned that this could dramatically double the 8-12in rise in sea levels already caused by climate change over the last century.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California rushes to prepare for massive ‘Kelvin’ wave and predicted sea level rise

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Insects provide protection, sanitation and even shelter to vertebrates, making them a priority for conservation efforts
For many vertebrates, insects are more than a food source. As “little things that run the world”, insects provide critical functions such as protection, sanitation and shelter across ecosystems, according to a new study.
The study, published in Nature Reviews Biodiversity on Wednesday, sheds light on the various ways insects support vertebrates, ranging from birds and bats to reptiles, amphibians and mammals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Insects play critical role in ecosystems beyond just providing food, new research shows

articles.author: Karen McVeigh
articles.description:
Fish and shellfish populations were falling rapidly as scallop dredgers devastated the seabed, but local activists and small-scale fishers battled hard to protect their coastline
Inside a bothy overlooking the Summer Isles, in the north-west of Scotland, the lilting tones of a traditional Gaelic duo fill a room full of musicians, storytellers, artists, local people and revellers, hung with fish-shaped lanterns and “Happy Birthday” signs.
It’s no ordinary birthday. The people in the small cabin have come together, on a windy night in Achiltibuie, a string of coastal hamlets and villages north of Ullapool, to celebrate an important milestone in the community’s history: a hard-won battle to protect their waters from the ravages of scallop dredging.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Beyond priceless’: how a halt to dredging saved the seas of Scotland’s Summer Isles

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Indigenous communities play crucial role, as ‘genetic bank’ area of wetland offers hope for critically endangered reptile
In the 1990s, conservationists in Cambodia feared the Siamese crocodile had disappeared for good. Fishing and hunting had devastated the species throughout the 20th century, leaving populations across its native south-east Asia on the brink of extinction.
But in villages dotted among the wetlands of the remote Cardamom mountains, Indigenous Chorng communities still reported seeing them. Passing this knowledge to researchers surveying the area in 2000 led to an official recording of the species – and bolstered the mission to revive the population.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saving the Siamese crocodile: Cambodia moves to protect one of the world’s last wild populations

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey with Miatta Fahnbulleh , produced by Nada Smiljanic and Zoe Hitch , the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Speaking to Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey at the Labour party conference in Liverpool, Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, said a mark of her success or failure would be whether she could get bills down and said she would do so. She also challenged Reform UK and the Tories on their climate inaction, saying they would eventually ‘bow’ because they were on the ‘wrong side of history’.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Labour bring down our energy bills? | Politics Weekly

articles.author: Gloria Dickie
articles.description:
Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answer
Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.
Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public. But in the past two years it has reached boiling point. A 2025 census found that the population had grown by a third since 2000, from 360 baboons to 493, now living in 12 managed troops.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
Hundreds of thousands are expected to die, millions to go hungry. This is not just about weather patterns, but about injustice
Some warnings are so grave that it is almost impossible to fully comprehend them. The descriptions of a super-sized, “Godzilla-level” El Niño already heating our planet would sound hyperbolic were they not issuing from eminent scientists. They say that the weather pattern, which occurs roughly every two to seven years, may be the strongest in at least a millennium. With its peak yet to come, the temperature rise in the Pacific Ocean has already surpassed the previous high.
The consequence will be huge amounts of heat in an atmosphere already experiencing frighteningly higher temperatures due to the human-caused climate crisis. Next year is almost certain to be the hottest on record globally, breaking this year’s record. The World Food Programme has warned that 50 million people are likely to be pushed into acute hunger. Others estimate that the extra heat from El Niño alone will cause the deaths of 450,000 people by February, from Nigeria and Indonesia to the US. That extraordinary toll is in addition to those killed by the wildfires, droughts and floods it is likely to bring – and also to deaths caused by global heating.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on a supersized El Niño: a natural phenomenon and human folly are a lethal combination | Editorial

articles.author: Nick Dall
articles.description:
Known as the ‘energy bars of the sea’ the fish are a key food source for many species, but closing fisheries to allow numbers to recover would cost millions 
It began on 28 July, when fishers near Saldanha Bay on the west coast of South Africa reported seeing dead sardines (also known as pilchards) floating at sea. Then, in early August, more dead sardines began washing up on beaches near Cape Town.
In the weeks that followed, similar reports came in from places across a vast area spanning 2,600km (1,600 miles) of coastline, such as Henties Bay in Namibia and Mbotyi in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa.

In the northern forests of the Congo-Brazzaville, as the sun slips away, a distinctive honking fills the dusky sky. Every evening, thousands of hammer-headed fruit bats depart their daytime roosts in search of mates, calling out through large, box-shaped snouts that give the flying mammals the appearance of a winged moose. Here, along the Congo River, scientists have been collecting DNA swabs and tissue samples from the bats for years, working deep into the night in spacesuit-like protective gear.
Those hard-won samples are now among the thousands of specimens gathered from bats across the world that have helped to reshape what we know about the bat family tree.

A magical film that explores the wonders of the deep sea through the eyes of a team of scientists and an underwater robot called Isis will be shown in selected cinemas across the UK next month.
The documentary, How Deep Is Your Love, offers a playful, irreverent and bittersweet look at our anthropocentric view of Earth, as it switches perspective from humans to deep sea animals and back again. It follows a research team from the Natural History Museum (NHM) in London, who sail for 12 days to reach a remote region called the Clarion Clipperton Zone, a biodiversity-rich area of the Pacific between Hawaii and Mexico. It takes Isis five hours to make the 3-mile (5km) descent to the bottom of this harsh world, where sunlight cannot penetrate, and where nodules rich in minerals mark it out as a hotspot for industrial mining.
